work.final:
I fixed `search.py` by replacing the helpers with proper logarithmic bisect helpers:

- `_bisect_left(items, value)` → smallest index where `items[i] >= value` (or `len(items)`).
- `_bisect_right(items, value)` → smallest index where `items[i] > value` (or `len(items)`).

Then each rule uses them:
- `find_first` = `_bisect_left`, returns it only if it lands on `value`, else -1.
- `find_last` = `_bisect_right - 1`, returns it only if it lands on `value`, else -1. This fixes the reported `find_last([1, 2, 2, 3], 3)` case.
- `count_of` = `_bisect_right - _bisect_left`, which is 0 when absent.
- `insert_position` = `_bisect_right`, inserting after any equal items (`[1,2,2,3]`, 2 → 3; 9 → 4).

All paths use half-open `[low, high)` ranges over `0..len(items)`, so empty, single-element, and out-of-range values all work without index errors, and each function runs in logarithmic time with no linear scanning.

queue.description:
# Fix the searches on a sorted list
`search.py` searches a list that is sorted in ascending order and may hold duplicates. A user reported:
> `find_last([1, 2, 2, 3], 3)` returns -1. The 3 is right there at the end.
Fix the module so that all four functions hold to these rules.
1. `find_first(items, value)` is the index of the first item equal to `value`, or -1.
2. `find_last(items, value)` is the index of the last item equal to `value`, or -1.
3. `count_of(items, value)` is how many items equal `value`.
4. `insert_position(items, value)` is the index at which `value` can be inserted **after** any equal items so that the list stays sorted. For `[1, 2, 2, 3]` and 2 it is 3, and for 9 it is 4.
5. All four work on the empty list, on a list of one item, and when `value` is smaller or larger than every item.
6. All four run in logarithmic time. Do not walk the list.
Run the provided tests with `python3 -m unittest test_visible -v`.
Acceptance criteria
Every rule in the description is implemented in search.py

The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
